'''Michael Peter Drazin''' (born 5 June 1929) is a British and American mathematician, working in [[noncommutative algebra]].

==Background==
The Drazins (Дразин) were a [[Russian Jewish]] family who moved to the United Kingdom in the years before [[World War I]]. Isaac Drazin founded in 1927 a well-known electrical goods shop in [[Heath Street, Hampstead|Heath Street]], [[Hampstead]], which existed for over 50 years.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Drazin |first1=Charles |title=Mapping the Past: A Search for Five Brothers at the Edge of Empire |date=25 August 2016 |publisher=Random House |isbn=978-1-4735-3842-9 |pages=8–9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QJsTDAAAQBAJ&pg=PA8 |language=en}}</ref> 

Isaac Drazin married Leah Wexler, and had three sons, of whom Michael was the eldest, and [[Philip Drazin]], also a mathematician, was the youngest, the middle son being David; and died 1 January 1993.<ref>Searches on the [https://www.freebmd.org.uk/ Free BDM site]</ref><ref>{{cite news | author       =<!--not stated-->|work=The Times |issue=64534 |page=16 |date=January 6, 1993}}</ref>

==Life==
Michael Drazin was born in London on 5 June 1929.<ref name="Press">{{cite book |last1=Press |first1=Jaques Cattell |title=American Men and Women of Science |date=1982 |publisher=Bowker |isbn=978-0-8352-1413-1 |page=712 |language=en}}</ref> His younger brother Philip was educated as a boarder at [[St Christopher School]], [[Letchworth]] during [[World War II]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Budd |first1=Chris |last2=Peregrine |first2=Howell |title=Philip Gerald Drazin |journal=Physics Today |date=1 March 2003 |volume=56 |issue=3 |pages=100–102 |doi=10.1063/1.1570792 |bibcode=2003PhT....56c.100B |issn=0031-9228|doi-access=free }}</ref> The self-published memoirs of Roger Atkinson, a school friend of Michael (Mike), indicate that Drazin attended [[King Alfred School, London]], located in [[Hampstead]], retaining contacts at the school when it was evacuated in wartime to [[Royston, Hertfordshire]]; Atkinson was a boarder at St Christopher School, Letchworth from September 1942. In 1946 Atkinson and Drazin visited Paris together.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Atkinson |first1=Roger |last2=Atkinson |first2=Catherine |title=Blackout, Austerity and Pride: Life in the 1940s |date=2015 |publisher=Roger Atkinson Publishing |isbn=978-0-9933007-0-7 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=N5lYjwEACAAJ |language=en}}</ref>

Drazin was a student at the [[University of Cambridge]], graduating B.A. in 1950 and M.A. in 1953.<ref name="Press"/> He was awarded a Ph.D. in 1953 for a dissertation ''Contributions to Abstract Algebra'' written with advisers [[Robert Rankin]] and [[David Rees (mathematician)|David Rees]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Drazin - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=16466 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref> He was a Fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] from 1952 to 1956, during that period relocating to the United States.<ref name="KS">{{cite book |last1=Kurz |first1=Heinz |last2=Salvadori |first2=Neri |title=Interpreting Classical Economics: Studies in Long-Period Analysis |date=12 July 2007 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-134-08781-5 |page=283 note 26 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v1d9AgAAQBAJ&pg=PT283 |language=en}}</ref>

In the academic year 1957–8 Drazin was Visiting Lecturer at [[Northwestern University]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=News and Notices |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |date=1958 |volume=65 |issue=1 |pages=60 |jstor=2310326 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2310326 |issn=0002-9890}}</ref> In 1958 he began a period at RIAS Inc. (the [[Research Institute for Advanced Studies]]) in [[Baltimore]] as senior scientist, after which he took a position as associate professor at [[Purdue University]] in 1962.<ref name="KS"/><ref>{{cite journal |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=5|issue=32 |page=432 |date=August 1958 |title=Personal Items |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/195808/195808FullIssue.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=9|issue=63 |page=376 |date=October 1962 |title=Personal Items |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/196210/196210FullIssue.pdf}}</ref>

==Works==
Drazin gave his name to a type of [[generalized inverse]] in [[ring theory]] and [[semigroup theory]] he introduced in 1958, now known as the [[Drazin inverse]]. It was later extended to contexts in [[operator theory]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Xue |first1=Yifeng |title=Stable Perturbations Of Operators And Related Topics |date=16 March 2012 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-4452-80-9 |page=133 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GAq7CgAAQBAJ&pg=PA133 |language=en}}</ref>

While at RIAS, Drazin worked with [[Emilie Virginia Haynsworth]], then at the [[National Bureau of Standards]], within its [[numerical analysis]] program.<ref>{{cite book |last1=United States National Bureau of Standards |title=National Bureau of Standards Report |date=1960 |publisher=The Bureau. |page=3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3ud6daHrbSQC&pg=PA3 |language=en}}</ref> He also worked with the metallurgist Henry Martin Otte of RIAS, and they published a book of crystallographic tables.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Otte |first1=Henry M. |title=Lattice Parameter Determinations with an X-Ray Spectrogoniometer by the Debye-Scherrer Method and the Effect of Specimen Condition |url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.1728392?journalCode=jap |journal=Journal of Applied Physics |pages=1536–1546 |doi=10.1063/1.1728392 |date=1 August 1961|volume=32 |issue=8 |bibcode=1961JAP....32.1536O |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Drazin |first1=M. P. |last2=Otte |first2=Henry Martin |title=Tables for Determining Cubic Crystal Orientations from Surface Traces of Octahedral Planes |date=1964 |publisher=P. M. Harrod Company |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RwokAQAAMAAJ |language=en}}</ref>
